activity_context.topic_title: Computing Partial Derivatives Using the Rules of Differentiation

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{h(x,y)}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)^{2}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡y\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡y\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
h(x,y)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$
